messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Adolescents and higher-weight children (aged 7 and older): Treatment starts at 10 mg/day, increasing to 20 mg/day after 2 weeks.
Additional dose increases may be considered after several more weeks if insufficient clinical improvement is observed.
The recommended dose range is 20 mg to 60 mg per day.
Lower-weight children: Treatment starts at 10 mg/day with dose increases after several more weeks if there is a lack of clinical improvement.
The recommended dose range is 20 mg to 30 mg per day.
Experience with daily doses greater than 20 mg is very minimal.
Bulimia Nervosa:
Adult dose: The recommended dose is 60 mg once daily in the morning.
Your doctor may gradually increase your dose to this level over several days.
Clinical trials showed that the 60 mg dose was effective.
The 60 mg dose was effective in reducing binge-eating and purging behaviors.
Panic Disorder:
Adult dose: Treatment starts at 10 mg/day, increasing to 20 mg/day after one week.
Your doctor may adjust the dose after several weeks if needed.
Clinical trials used a dose range of 10 mg/day to 60 mg/day.
Triples: [["Fluoxetine", "has recommended dose", "10 mg/day for adolescents and higher-weight children"], ["Fluoxetine", "has dose increase instruction", "increase to 20 mg/day after 2 weeks for adolescents and higher-weight children"], ["Fluoxetine", "has dose increase instruction", "additional dose increases after several more weeks if insufficient clinical improvement"], ["Fluoxetine", "has recommended dose range", "20 mg to 60 mg per day for adolescents and higher-weight children"], ["Fluoxetine", "has recommended dose", "10 mg/day for lower-weight children"], ["Fluoxetine", "has dose increase instruction", "dose increases after several more weeks if there is a lack of clinical improvement for lower-weight children"], ["Fluoxetine", "has recommended dose range", "20 mg to 30 mg per day for lower-weight children"], ["Fluoxetine", "has warning", "experience with daily doses greater than 20 mg is very minimal"], ["Fluoxetine", "has recommended dose", "60 mg once daily in the morning for bulimia nervosa"], ["Fluoxetine", "has dose adjustment instruction", "doctor may gradually increase dose to this level over several days for bulimia nervosa"], ["Fluoxetine", "has clinical trial result", "60 mg dose was effective for bulimia nervosa"], ["Fluoxetine", "has clinical trial result", "60 mg dose was effective in reducing binge-eating and purging behaviors for bulimia nervosa"], ["Fluoxetine", "has recommended dose", "10 mg/day for panic disorder"], ["Fluoxetine", "has dose increase instruction", "increase to 20 mg/day after one week for panic disorder"], ["Fluoxetine", "has dose adjustment instruction", "doctor may adjust dose after several weeks if needed for panic disorder"], ["Fluoxetine", "has clinical trial dose range", "10 mg/day to 60 mg/day for panic disorder"]]
Relations: ["has clinical trial dose range", "has clinical trial result", "has dose adjustment instruction", "has dose increase instruction", "has recommended dose", "has recommended dose range", "has warning"]
Answer:

completion:
has clinical trial dose range: The subject drug was tested in clinical trials using the dose range specified by the object entity.  
has clinical trial result: The subject drug demonstrated the clinical outcome or effect specified by the object entity in clinical trials.  
has dose adjustment instruction: The subject drug may require the dosage adjustment specified by the object entity under certain conditions.  
has dose increase instruction: The subject drug may require the dosage increase specified by the object entity under certain conditions.  
has recommended dose: The subject drug is recommended to be administered at the dose specified by the object entity.  
has recommended dose range: The subject drug is recommended to be administered within the dose range specified by the object entity.  
has warning: The subject drug has a caution or warning related to the information specified by the object entity.
